Sara — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. I reviewed the doc and pulled out the two commercial items so we can resolve quickly: invoice remit + net terms.

Quick answers & proposals:
- Invoice remit: we can route invoices to Stellix Inc. (US) provided we have the BU wiring details and a remit-to PO number. We will add a short invoice recipient field in Exhibit A that our billing team will follow. Can you confirm the exact remit entity name and tax id?
- Net terms: our standard is Net 30 for hosted subscriptions; for larger annual commitments we can agree to Net 45 with a 1.5% processing fee for the extended terms. Alternatively, we can offer a milestone invoice cadence that preserves Net 30 on each invoice (staged billing). Which does your finance team prefer?

Markus (legal) — can you confirm the suggested language for tax/withholding and whether we should keep the current indemnity clause or propose a narrow carve-out for VAT reverse charge?

I attached an internal copy of the redline and flagged the lines where billing changes are needed. If it's helpful, recommend a 30-minute call today or tomorrow to lock the invoice flow so finance can sign off.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations (Contracts & Pricing)
Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 12:14:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Initial Order Form redline and billing questions

Forwarding Sara's redline with my notes inline — see below. High level: keep contract language tight on tax gross-up and withholdings; we should not accept open-ended indemnities tied to tax policy changes. I propose the following clause for Section 6 (Taxes):

"Each party shall bear its own taxes. Where applicable VAT/GST is chargeable on Redwood's invoices, Redwood will charge VAT in accordance with the law of the invoicing jurisdiction. Customer will provide valid evidence where reverse charge applies; absent valid evidence, Customer shall reimburse Redwood for VAT charged back to Redwood by tax authorities."

Regarding remit and net terms: if we accept Net 45 we should add a provisioning that Redwood may invoice an early termination adjustment if payment delays extend beyond 90 days. Also, the 1.5% processing fee for Net 45 is standard practice; alternatively, staged invoice cadence is lower friction for compliance.

I've suggested specific redlines in the attached doc and added comment tags at Art. 2.1 (invoice recipient) and Art. 3.2 (payment schedule).

Markus Klein
VP Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_Stellix_Redline_v2.docx (legal comments added)

Markus / Kim — thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed your proposed tax language and the invoice recipient approach. A few points from our side:
- We can provide evidence for reverse charge in most EU jurisdictions, but for the US entity remit we need to keep the contract signed by the group parent (Stellix Ltd) and make clear the invoice recipient is Stellix Inc. Our tax team will supply the US tax id and remit-to address by EOD tomorrow.
- Net terms: CFO is open to Net 45 but will not accept a processing fee. Instead we propose two adjustments: (1) a Net 45 without fee for the first year with a performance-based true-up at renewal; (2) if Redwood requires immediate cashflow coverage, Stellix can accept a staged billing schedule (50% upfront, remainder quarterly).

I attached an updated commercial schedule reflecting the staged option (Commercial_Schedule_v3.xlsx).

We are available for a call tomorrow 10:00–11:30 PT. Please confirm and we will put finance on the line.

Regards,
